item.title: New study traces evolution of terrestrial animals on Qinghai-Xizang Plateau
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30
CHENGDU, Oct. 30 (Xinhua) -- A new study has reconstructed the evolutionary history of terrestrial animals on the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau, offering a clearer picture of how the unique fauna of Earth's "Third Pole" took shape over millions of years. The research, led by a team from the Chengdu Institute of Biology (CIB) under the Chinese Academy of Sciences, was recently published in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS). "Overall, the study deepens understanding of how mountain animal life evolves and provides a framework for studying how biodiversity forms in mountain regions worldwide," said Li Jiatang, a researcher at CIB. Home to many species found nowhere else, the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau is one of the world's biodiversity hotspots, covering about 3.07 million square kilometers and ranging in elevation from 88 to 8,848 meters, according to the researchers. The plateau platform, the Himalayas and the Hengduan Mountains are the plateau's three major subregions. Scientists have long been interested in how the plateau's tectonic history and monsoon systems shaped the evolution of local biodiversity. However, earlier studies mostly looked at plants or single animal groups, leaving the overall development of the plateau's land animals poorly understood. To fill this gap, the researchers combined time-calibrated evolutionary trees covering more than 20,000 species across invertebrates, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals. They then reconstructed the evolutionary history of 527 endemic terrestrial animal species on the plateau. The study found that most of the plateau's endemic land animals did not arrive from elsewhere and then become new species. Instead, many evolved locally, splitting into new species right where they were, something scientists call in situ diversification. The plateau was also a major receiver of species. The study found that animals moved in nearly twice as often as they moved out. The Qinghai-Xizang Plateau therefore played two roles at once: it was a place where new species formed, and a biogeographic sink that took in more species than it sent out. The three subregions played very different roles. The Hengduan Mountains were the main source of local species formation, producing many new species. The Himalayas were both a source and a sink, producing new species locally and receiving species from elsewhere. The plateau platform produced very few new species locally, with most of its animal life coming from immigration, making it an important sink and a major receiver of species. The researchers also examined how geology and climate shaped this evolutionary history. They found that a major climate transition about 34 million years ago marked the onset of sustained species diversification and biological exchange. However, the timing of these processes varied across the three subregions, reflecting differences in their uplift histories and monsoon systems. The study also found a consistent "plants first, animals later" pattern. By comparing animal evolution with plant studies, the researchers identified this pattern across the plateau and its subregions. Early-colonizing plant groups created suitable ecological niches, laying the foundation for later animal immigration and diversification. ■

item.title: The one-person company, the port and the shopping bag, snapshots from Hainan FTP
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30
A reach stacker lifts a container at Yangpu Port in Danzhou City, south China's Hainan Province, Oct. 21, 2026. (Xinhua/Wang Teng) by Xinhua writer Wang Teng HAIKOU, Oct. 30 (Xinhua) -- At dusk, the salty sea air drifted over a beach on south China's Hainan Island, where a young man sat alone. The man, Li Baihong, founded a one-person company (OPC) specializing in software development. Unlike traditional ventures, an OPC is usually led by a single entrepreneur with AI tools handling tasks that would otherwise require a larger team. His "employees" are three laptops loaded with AI assistants helping him develop software. Now, he has earned about 200,000 yuan (about 30,000 U.S. dollars) in six months since the company was established. In April this year, he resigned from a leading Chinese internet company in Shanghai and flew to Hainan with his belongings in three suitcases. "I've explored several OPC communities in cities such as Hangzhou and Shenzhen. But I chose Hainan because the working environment here is like a forest park," said Li, adding that his happiest moment each day is the 10-minute e-bike ride to the seaside after work. On the day he landed in Hainan, he submitted the documents to the local authorities online and received his business license seven days later. Li's company is based in Hainan Free Trade Port Resort Software Community, just a 10-minute e-bike ride from the beach. The community offers entrepreneurship coaching, rent-free offices, and funding for entrepreneurs. Under Hainan Free Trade Port (FTP) policies, eligible companies can benefit from a preferential corporate income tax rate of 15 percent. "I used to earn a high salary in Shanghai, but the taxes were high as well. So, the tax rate is one of the factors I consider when running my own company," he said. To date, the community has attracted more than 400 AI-powered OPC enterprise entities and 700 makers, as well as entrepreneurs from overseas, said Si Xinying, director of Chengmai Digital Economy Research Institute, which is based in this community. As the sun sank below the horizon, Li was still sitting on the beach. Lights came on at a port in the distance, and the sound of a ship's horn drifted in. The next day, I took a bus along the western stretch of the Hainan Island loop road and reached Yangpu Port, the largest cargo port in the Hainan FTP. When I arrived, customs officers were inspecting a shipment of coconuts imported from Thailand. Using intelligent inspection equipment, customs can complete inspection of a single shipment in under three minutes. "If the machine detects abnormalities, the shipment will be sent for manual inspection," said Zeng Jie, deputy head of the supervision department of Yangpu Port Customs. Since last December, the Hainan FTP launched island-wide special customs operations, a system that treats the whole island as a special customs area. As of Oct. 22, the Yangpu border inspection station has inspected 4,104 inbound and outbound vessels, up 11.95 percent year on year. Among the goods unloaded from Yangpu Port are shipments sent to Hainan's duty-free shops. Currently, 12 offshore duty-free shops are located across Hainan Island. Sanya City was the final stop on my reporting trip to Hainan. On the last day, after booking my departure ticket, I went to the Sanya International Duty Free Shopping Complex to buy duty-free goods for my family. The sprawling mall offers a wide selection of international brands, attractive duty-free prices and convenient pickup services. Tourists holding departure tickets from Hainan Island, including but not limited to train, ship or airplane tickets, may purchase duty-free goods in any duty-free shop on the island. After payment, they can take the goods with them or choose to have them delivered. "Since the launch of special customs operations, foreign tourists who meet the requirements and plan to leave the island and the country can enjoy a tax exemption of 100,000 yuan per year to buy duty-free goods in Hainan, like other Chinese tourists," introduced Zhang Bin, general manager of China Duty Free Group Sanya Downtown Duty Free Store Co., Ltd. There, I met a tourist from Russia carrying several shopping bags. She told me that it was her first time visiting China. "It feels wonderful, because I can enjoy the island's tropical coastal scenery and buy international goods at such great prices," she said. From January to September 2026, Haikou Customs supervised duty-free sales worth about 16.29 billion yuan in Sanya, with about 2.4 million shopper visits and about 12.59 million items purchased, up 16.48 percent, 6.29 percent, and 6.24 percent year on year, respectively. After shopping, I headed to the airport. When the plane took off, I could see the golden beach and the cerulean sea outside the window. Although my trip has come to an end, the story of Hainan FTP continues. ■

item.title: Economic Watch: China pushes ahead with urban renewal to upgrade city life, unlock growth potential
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30
BEIJING, Oct. 30 (Xinhua) -- Zhang Laiyuan, a longtime resident in a run-down neighborhood in east China, recalled the days of family reunion dinners in the past: "The living room was so small that half of us had to sit on the bed to eat." In Shiliu New Village, Nanjing, capital of Jiangsu Province, windows once directly faced those of neighboring homes, roofs leaked frequently, and many residents had no indoor toilets. This residential compound dates back to the 1950s. Roughly 1,500 residents were once packed onto a 16,000-square-meter plot. Nearly half the units spanned less than 35 square meters, with the smallest measuring a mere seven square meters. The compound has been rebuilt from the ground up, with the first phase of 282 units completed and handed over last year. Every building now features not only standard amenities -- elevators, independent kitchens, bathrooms and balconies -- but also smart security systems, fire safety equipment and barrier-free ramps, along with underground parking, community commercial space, greenery and recreational plazas. Last Spring Festival, Zhang's daughter, son-in-law and granddaughter came back for the holiday. The whole family sat together in the new living room, with plenty of space to spare. UPGRADING AGING HOUSING TO MODERN STANDARDS The transformation of Shiliu New Village mirrors what is taking place across cities in China. Following decades of fast-paced urbanization progress, aging housing stock now makes up a substantial portion of China's real estate market. In response, experts say the focus of urban development has shifted away from large-scale expansion to improving the quality of existing housing stock. Many cities are exploring ways to bring aging housing up to modern living standards, including complete demolition and reconstruction as well as micro-renovation. The goal is to systematically address issues ranging from safety risks and outdated layouts to inadequate accessibility for elderly residents. In an old courtyard in Beijing's Chaoyang District, workers replaced rotting wooden roof structures with durable steel ones using prefabrication techniques. In Shanghai's Hongkou District, an apartment block was rebuilt with steel frames and prefabricated components, allowing residents to stay in their community throughout construction. The central government has allocated 97 billion yuan (about 14.45 billion U.S. dollars) in its 2026 budget for urban renewal, mainly for renovating old and dilapidated urban housing, and the funding is expected to benefit around eight million households. Under the national urban renewal plan (2026-2030) released earlier this year, China aims to launch renovations on 115,000 old urban residential compounds, retrofit or install 575,000 residential elevators, and build or upgrade 50,000 hectares of urban green space. ECOLOGY, INDUSTRY, CONSUMPTION AS NEW PRIORITIES The Maozhou River in south China's Guangdong Province was once heavily polluted. Following vigorous pollution control and vegetation restoration by local authorities in Shenzhen, the river has been transformed into a leisure belt with six ecological wetlands and 45.6 kilometers of walking trails. Rowing and dragon boat activities have also been introduced. Zheng Degao, vice president of the China Academy of Urban Planning and Design, said river regulation has gone beyond conventional environmental protection to take on a new meaning -- reshaping urban waterfront spaces to activate the whole city. According to the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development, between 2026 and 2030, China will renovate or upgrade 20,000 hectares of urban parkland, add 15,000 mini-sized "pocket parks" and build or upgrade 20,000 kilometers of urban greenways. Urban renewal also holds huge potential for investment and consumption. China has set a target of renovating 1,500 old streets and factory compounds from 2026 to 2030, bringing in new industries and business models to inject fresh momentum into urban development. Experts estimate the total urban renewal market will reach 15 trillion to 20 trillion yuan over the 2026-2030 period. A renewal project in Shanghai's Xuhui District preserves the industrial heritage of a cement plant, an airport and a railway station while creating media and digital and intelligence industry clusters. More than 4,000 companies covering multiple sectors including artificial intelligence have gathered here, generating over 150,000 new jobs. "Converting old streets and factory sites into cultural and creative districts drives growth in dining, retail and entertainment, while upgraded parks and sports facilities open new consumption scenarios for families, seniors and leisure seekers," said Yan Yuejin, deputy director of the E-house China R&D Institute. Urban renewal is injecting lasting momentum into high-quality urban development while opening up broad opportunities for the real economy and capital markets, he said. ■

item.title: Xi plays decisive role in drafting CPC leadership's resolution on full, rigorous Party self-governance: official
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30
BEIJING, Oct. 30 (Xinhua) -- Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, has played a decisive role in drafting the Party leadership's Resolution of the Central Committee of the CPC on Certain Major Issues concerning Persevering with Full and Rigorous Party Self-Governance, a senior official said Friday. Hailing the resolution as the most important outcome of the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee, Tang Fangyu, head of the Policy Research Office of the CPC Central Committee, said the drafting of the resolution was carried out under the leadership of the CPC Central Committee, with Xi acting as the chief of the document drafting group, personally planning, guiding throughout the process, and setting the overall vision. Tang made the remarks at a press conference on the guiding principles from the just-concluded plenum, which was held in Beijing from Oct. 26 to 29. According to Tang, the document outlines the importance, urgency, and overall requirements of persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance, and lays out specific plans for related work in seven parts. The document also includes content on refining Party and state oversight systems and ensuring the implementation of the political responsibility for full and rigorous Party self-governance, Tang said. ■

item.title: Xi stresses Party self-governance to ensure CPC remains strong leadership core
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30
BEIJING, Oct. 30 (Xinhua) -- Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, stressed the need to persevere with full and rigorous Party self-governance to ensure that the CPC remains the strong leadership core in advancing socialism with Chinese characteristics. Xi made the remarks at a symposium on Aug. 21 to solicit opinions from non-Party personages on drafting the resolution of the CPC Central Committee on certain major issues concerning persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance. The resolution was adopted at the fifth plenary session of the 20th Central Committee of the CPC, which concluded on Thursday in Beijing. ■

item.title: CPC plenum concludes, adopting resolution on persevering with full, rigorous Party self-governance
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-29
Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, delivers an important address at the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee in Beijing, capital of China. The 20th CPC Central Committee held its fifth plenary session in Beijing from Oct. 26 to Oct. 29, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) BEIJING, Oct. 29 (Xinhua) -- The 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC) held its fifth plenary session from Monday to Thursday in Beijing, adopting a resolution on persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance. The Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee presided over the meeting. Xi Jinping, general secretary of the CPC Central Committee, delivered an important address, said a communique issued after the session. At the session, participants heard and discussed a report on the work of the Political Bureau presented by Xi. They also considered and adopted the Resolution of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China on Certain Major Issues concerning Persevering with Full and Rigorous Party Self-Governance. Xi delivered explanatory remarks on the draft of the resolution. The CPC Central Committee fully affirmed the work of the Political Bureau since the committee's fourth plenary session, the communique said. Looking back on the Party's journey since its founding, the CPC Central Committee pointed out that the key to the success of the CPC in winning one victory after another lies in its pursuit of the high ideal of communism, its dedication to achieving lasting greatness for the Chinese nation, and its commitment to seeking happiness for the Chinese people and rejuvenation for the Chinese nation. At the session, the CPC Central Committee gave a highly positive assessment of the great achievements the Party has made in exercising full and rigorous self-governance in the new era. It was pointed out that as the Party endeavors to supervise, govern, develop, and strengthen itself in the new era, the CPC Central Committee with Comrade Xi Jinping at its core has put forward a series of new ideas, new thinking, and new strategies in response to the major questions of the times -- what kind of long-term governing Marxist party the CPC should build and how to build it, thereby giving rise to Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building. "It was stressed that many favorable conditions are now in place for advancing full and rigorous Party self-governance, while we also face many new circumstances and new issues in this endeavor," the communique said. Profound changes in global, national, and Party conditions have made the CPC's tasks of uniting and leading the people in safeguarding China's sovereignty, security, and development interests, of uniting and leading the people in promoting reform and development and maintaining social harmony and stability, and of maintaining its advanced nature and integrity even more formidable, it added. "Dedicated to fulfilling the Party's missions and tasks, we must act in line with the overall requirements for Party building in the new era, take the Party Constitution as our fundamental guide, maintain the Party's vanguard nature, and uphold the overall leadership of the Party and the centralized, unified leadership of the Party Central Committee," the communique said. At the session, the guiding principles for persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance were highlighted as follows: serving the Party's missions and tasks; taking strengthening the Party politically as the overarching principle; exercising rigorous governance across the board; adopting a problem-oriented approach; upholding fundamental principles and breaking new ground; adhering to a top-down approach; and running the Party according to regulations. Systematic plans for persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance were also made at the session, according to the communique. Strengthening the Party spirit represents a fundamental task in the CPC's efforts to ensure full and rigorous Party self-governance, it said. Democratic centralism is the Party's fundamental organizational principle and leadership system, and its implementation is therefore an inherent requirement for exercising full and rigorous Party self-governance, the communique added. Strict management of officials is the key to full and rigorous Party self-governance, it noted. "We will build up the ranks of high-caliber officials with firm political commitment, outstanding professional competence, excellent work conduct, and strict discipline," it added. Party organizations at all levels play the principal role in exercising full and rigorous Party self-governance, said the communique, adding that it is therefore essential to systematically advance the development of Party organizations at all levels and in all sectors to strengthen their political and organizational functions. Improving conduct and tightening discipline are effective measures to advance full and rigorous Party self-governance, said the communique. "It was noted that taking integrated steps to ensure that officials do not have the audacity, opportunity, or desire to commit corruption is both an important strategy for full and rigorous Party self-governance and a fundamental guideline for our fight against corruption," the communique said. "We must take systematic steps to address both symptoms and root causes of corruption and adopt a holistic approach that combines severe punishment, targeted remedy, and effective prevention, carrying this fight through to the end," it stated. Strengthening Party regulations and institutions represents a long-term, fundamental strategy for ensuring full and rigorous Party self-governance, said the communique. Persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance entails further improvement to Party and state oversight systems, said the communique, adding that it is the common political responsibility of all Party members. Studying and implementing the guiding principles from this plenary session represent a major political task for the entire Party both at present and in the period to come, according to the communique. It was also stressed that all aspects of the Party's work agenda should be steadily advanced at the turn of the year. The CPC Central Committee decided at the session that the Party will convene its 21st National Congress in Beijing in the second half of 2027 and stated that this congress, which is to be held at a critical stage for basically realizing socialist modernization and on a new journey toward the Second Centenary Goal, will be a highly important meeting and an event of great political significance for both the Party and the country. The session elected Zhang Shengmin as a new member of the CPC Central Committee Political Bureau, according to the communique. The session also decided on the filling of empty seats on the Central Committee by alternate members, deliberated and adopted inspection reports of the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection and the Central Military Commission on those committing grave violations of discipline and laws, and confirmed the Political Bureau's previous decisions to punish those violators. The CPC Central Committee called upon the entire Party to rally more closely around the CPC Central Committee with Xi at its core and fully implement Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. ■ The fifth plenary session of the 20th Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee is presided over by the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee in Beijing, capital of China.
